topic: Your keyboard layout (QWERTY) is over 150 years old
pillar: Present: how things got this way

claims.claim: 1874 falls within the Victorian era (Queen Victoria's reign, 1837-1901), so the layout is literally Victorian.
QWERTY is named after the first six letters on the top letter row.
The layout comes from the Sholes & Glidden Type-Writer, released by E. Remington & Sons in 1874 (over 150 years ago).
Christopher Latham Sholes and colleagues changed the key arrangement many times over several years of prototypes.
Why the layout ended up this way is debated: the popular typebar-jamming explanation is contested (one study links it to telegraph operators).
claims.note: Script says 'historians still argue' - no causal claim either way.

claims.claim: In 1893 major typewriter makers including Remington merged into the Union Typewriter Company, which made QWERTY the standard.

rejected.claim: QWERTY was designed to slow typists down.
'TYPEWRITER' can be typed on the top row as a sales trick.
